status: method specification committed before Phase 8 scoring; all LoCoMo and LongMemEval outcomes from prior stages have already been seen, so Phase 8 is exploratory
research_question: Can immutable, causal turn-arrival segmentation preserve evidence retrieval under the same text budget as retrospective lexical event and fixed-turn segmentation?
datasets: pinned LoCoMo with Phase 1 eligibility, 3 development and 7 previously examined held-out conversations
pinned LongMemEval-S cleaned, 470 answerable records under Phase 7 label audit, as descriptive external check

causal_writer.input: turn text and session boundary only; no future turns, query, labels, summaries, roles, or dates
causal_writer.tokenization: Phase 2 lowercase Unicode regex word tokens
causal_writer.novelty: 1 - Jaccard(set(current-turn tokens), union of sets of the previous three turns in the same session); if both sets empty, novelty is zero; no idf fit
causal_writer.boundary_order: before accepting turn t, close the current open segment if adding t exceeds 160 words, else close if open has at least 64 words and novelty >= 0.85; then append t; close remainder at session end
causal_writer.oversized_turn: an individual >160-word turn is stored whole; close before next turn
causal_writer.immutability: closed segments never change; a boundary recognized on arrival of t may close the previous segment at t, with no lookahead beyond t
causal_writer.memory_scope: only final segment index is queried after the full history; streaming retrieval or answer generation is not measured

comparators: Phase 3 frozen retrospective lexical event, w3, min64/preferred128/max160
full session as contextual baseline on LoCoMo
ranker: unchanged Phase 2 BM25 and whole-segment skip-if-over-budget retrieval
primary_outcome: question-level all annotated evidence turn IDs in selected segments at 1024 words
primary_comparison: causal writer versus Phase 3 retrospective lexical event on 599 previously examined LoCoMo held-out questions, paired by conversation
secondary: segment counts, word sizes and boundaries
prefix invariance and no-future input tests
interpretation: all outcomes exploratory, including the reused held-out set; evidence retrieval is not generated-answer accuracy, psychological event-boundary quality, or meaning in Searle's sense
